Definition: or δῦμι prolonged forms of an obsolete primary δύο (to sink); to go "down":--set.
BiblicalUsage: To set, of the sun, as when the sun was setting, all who had any sick brought them to Jesus, and He laid His hands on every one of them and healed them.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the setting sun was the signal for the healing to begin, because the day's work ended and the Saviour's work went on into the night.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
